-- dim_date: one row per calendar day, covering whole calendar years around every date the facts use.
-- Port of sql/dimensions/dim_date.sql. Role-played by the facts (purchase, approved, carrier, delivered,
-- estimated, shipping limit, review dates).
-- Grain: one row per day. Key: date_key = yyyymmdd (smart key); -1 = not applicable (missing date).
-- Built from a generated calendar, not from order dates: 2016-11 has no orders but must still exist.
--
-- Snowflake notes
--   * the day spine comes from GENERATOR; seq4() can have gaps, so it is re-numbered with row_number()
--   * MONTHNAME()/DAYNAME() return abbreviations in Snowflake, so full English names are spelled out with
--     DECODE on month() / dayofweekiso() (locale independent)
--   * DuckDB weekofyear() is the ISO week -> weekiso()
with seen as (
    select order_purchase_timestamp::date       as d from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__orders
    union all select order_approved_at::date              from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__orders
    union all select order_delivered_carrier_date::date   from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__orders
    union all select order_delivered_customer_date::date  from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__orders
    union all select order_estimated_delivery_date::date  from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__orders
    union all select shipping_limit_date::date            from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__order_items
    union all select review_creation_date::date           from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__order_reviews
    union all select review_answer_timestamp::date        from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__order_reviews
),

bounds as (
    select
        date_trunc('year', min(d))::date                                   as first_day,
        dateadd(day, -1, dateadd(year, 1, date_trunc('year', max(d))))::date as last_day
    from seen
),

spine as (
    -- 10,000 candidate days (~27 years) is far more than the 2016-2020 window; the singular test
    -- dim_date_covers_all_used_dates fails if the spine is ever too short.
    select row_number() over (order by seq4()) - 1 as n
    from table(generator(rowcount => 10000))
),

days as (
    select dateadd(day, spine.n, bounds.first_day)::date as d
    from spine
    cross join bounds
    where dateadd(day, spine.n, bounds.first_day) <= bounds.last_day
)

select
    cast(-1 as integer)                  as date_key,
    cast(null as date)                   as full_date,
    cast(null as integer)                as year,
    cast(null as integer)                as quarter,
    cast(null as integer)                as month,
    cast('Not applicable' as varchar)    as month_name,
    cast('Not applicable' as varchar)    as year_month,
    cast(null as integer)                as day_of_month,
    cast(null as integer)                as iso_week,
    cast(null as integer)                as day_of_week,
    cast('Not applicable' as varchar)    as day_name,
    cast(null as boolean)                as is_weekend

union all

select
    to_char(d, 'YYYYMMDD')::integer                                  as date_key,
    d                                                                as full_date,
    year(d)                                                          as year,
    quarter(d)                                                       as quarter,
    month(d)                                                         as month,
    decode(month(d),
        1, 'January', 2, 'February', 3, 'March', 4, 'April', 5, 'May', 6, 'June',
        7, 'July', 8, 'August', 9, 'September', 10, 'October', 11, 'November', 12, 'December'
    )                                                                as month_name,
    to_char(d, 'YYYY-MM')                                            as year_month,
    day(d)                                                           as day_of_month,
    weekiso(d)                                                       as iso_week,
    dayofweekiso(d)                                                  as day_of_week,
    decode(dayofweekiso(d),
        1, 'Monday', 2, 'Tuesday', 3, 'Wednesday', 4, 'Thursday', 5, 'Friday', 6, 'Saturday', 7, 'Sunday'
    )                                                                as day_name,
    dayofweekiso(d) >= 6                                             as is_weekend
from days

-- int_customers_latest: one row per real customer (customer_unique_id) with location attributes taken from
-- the customer's most recent order (type-1). Logic lifted from sql/dimensions/dim_customer.sql.
-- customer_id is per ORDER in the source, so it is only used here to find the latest order.
-- Tie-break (identical to DuckDB): latest purchase timestamp first, NULL purchase timestamps last
-- (explicit NULLS LAST: Snowflake would otherwise put NULLs first under DESC), then customer_id ascending.
with ranked as (
    select
        c.customer_unique_id,
        c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
        c.customer_city,
        c.customer_state,
        row_number() over (
            partition by c.customer_unique_id
            order by o.order_purchase_timestamp desc nulls last, c.customer_id
        ) as rn
    from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__customers c
    left join RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__orders o
        on o.customer_id = c.customer_id
)

select
    customer_unique_id,
    customer_zip_code_prefix,
    customer_city,
    customer_state
from ranked
where rn = 1

    cast('UNKNOWN' as varchar)           as product_id,

    cast(null as bigint)                 as product_volume_cm3

union all

select
    cast(row_number() over (order by p.product_id) as bigint)                        as product_key,
    p.product_id,
    coalesce(p.product_category_name, 'unknown')                                     as product_category_name,
    coalesce(t.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name, 'unknown')    as product_category_name_english,

-- int_geography_rollup: one row per zip-code prefix. Logic lifted from sql/dimensions/dim_geography.sql.
--   * latitude / longitude = median of the in-bounds points
--   * state / city = most frequent value, ties broken alphabetically (8 prefixes span more than one state).
--     The sort is a binary (code-point) comparison in both DuckDB and Snowflake's default collation.
-- NULL city/state values are counted as their own group, exactly as the DuckDB GROUP BY does.
-- Rank with row_number() over pre-counted groups (rather than a window over an aggregate) so the ordering is explicit.
with coords as (
    select
        zip_prefix,
        median(lat)  as latitude,
        median(lng)  as longitude,
        count(*)     as n_points
    from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_INTERMEDIATE.int_geography_points
    group by zip_prefix
),

state_counts as (
    select zip_prefix, state, count(*) as n
    from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_INTERMEDIATE.int_geography_points
    group by zip_prefix, state
),

top_state as (
    select zip_prefix, state
    from state_counts
    qualify row_number() over (partition by zip_prefix order by n desc, state) = 1
),

city_counts as (
    select zip_prefix, city, count(*) as n
    from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_INTERMEDIATE.int_geography_points
    group by zip_prefix, city
),

top_city as (
    select zip_prefix, city
    from city_counts
    qualify row_number() over (partition by zip_prefix order by n desc, city) = 1
)

select
    c.zip_prefix,
    tc.city,
    ts.state,
    c.latitude,
    c.longitude,
    c.n_points
from coords c
join top_state ts on ts.zip_prefix = c.zip_prefix
join top_city  tc on tc.zip_prefix = c.zip_prefix

-- Singular test: returns the rows where expected and actual differ (a passing test returns zero rows).
-- Port of check 22 in sql/validation/checks.sql: dim_date contains all 30 days of 2016-11 (a month with no orders; a calendar fact, not an EDA constant)
-- Expectations are derived from the staging models, never hard-coded EDA constants.
-- `is distinct from` makes a NULL expected/actual value fail instead of silently passing.
select expected, actual
from (
    select
        (select 30) as expected,
        (select count(*) from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_MARTS.dim_date where year_month = '2016-11')   as actual
)

-- whole calendar years (first day = 1 January of the earliest used year, last day = 31 December of the latest).
-- Guards the GENERATOR spine in dim_date.sql against ever being too short. Returns the failing rows.
with seen as (
    select order_purchase_timestamp::date       as d from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__orders
    union all select order_approved_at::date              from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__orders
    union all select order_delivered_carrier_date::date   from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_STAGING.stg_olist__orders

    from RETAIL_OLIST.DBT_CI_MARTS.dim_date

            || to_char(have_first, 'YYYY-MM-DD') || '..' || to_char(have_last, 'YYYY-MM-DD') || ' found' as detail
    from span
    cross join have
    where want_first is distinct from have_first

-- Grain: one row per order_id. Order-level process measures: lifecycle dates, delivery time, lateness.
-- Items and payments are pre-aggregated to the order grain BEFORE joining (int_order_items_agg,
-- int_order_payments_agg): joining them side by side would repeat rows and overstate item revenue by ~4.5-5%.
-- Missing milestone dates map to date_key -1 (not applicable); the raw timestamps stay nullable.
--
-- Snowflake notes
--   * date_diff('second', a, b) / 86400.0  ->  datediff(second, a, b)::float / 86400.0  (float, not NUMBER scale)
--   * sums are cast back to number(12,2) because Snowflake widens SUM() to NUMBER(38,2)
select
    o.order_id,
    o.customer_id,
    o.order_status,
    cast(coalesce(dc.customer_key, -1) as bigint)               as customer_key,
    cast(coalesce(g.geography_key, -1) as bigint)               as customer_geography_key,
    coalesce(to_char(o.order_purchase_timestamp, 'YYYYMMDD')::integer, -1)                as purchase_date_key,
    coalesce(to_char(o.order_approved_at, 'YYYYMMDD')::integer, -1)                        as approved_date_key,
    coalesce(to_char(o.order_delivered_carrier_date, 'YYYYMMDD')::integer, -1)            as carrier_date_key,
    coalesce(to_char(o.order_delivered_customer_date, 'YYYYMMDD')::integer, -1)           as delivered_customer_date_key,
    coalesce(to_char(o.order_estimated_delivery_date, 'YYYYMMDD')::integer, -1)           as estimated_delivery_date_key,
    o.order_purchase_timestamp                                  as purchase_ts,
    o.order_approved_at                                         as approved_ts,
    o.order_delivered_carrier_date                              as carrier_ts,
    o.order_delivered_customer_date                             as delivered_customer_ts,
    o.order_estimated_delivery_date                             as estimated_delivery_ts,
    cast(coalesce(i.item_count, 0) as integer)                  as item_count,           -- 0 for orders with no items
    cast(coalesce(i.items_price, 0) as number(12, 2))           as items_price,
    cast(coalesce(i.items_freight, 0) as number(12, 2))         as items_freight,
    cast(coalesce(p.payment_count, 0) as integer)               as payment_count,
    cast(coalesce(p.payment_total, 0) as number(12, 2))         as payment_total,
    -- purchase -> customer delivery, fractional days
    datediff(second, o.order_purchase_timestamp, o.order_delivered_customer_date)::float / 86400.0

    -- delivered - estimated; positive = late

                                                                as delivery_delay_days,
    -- delivered after the estimate; NULL if no delivery date
    o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date
                                                                as is_late,
    -- carrier before purchase, or customer before carrier
    (
        coalesce(o.order_delivered_carrier_date < o.order_purchase_timestamp, false)
        or coalesce(o.order_delivered_customer_date < o.order_delivered_carrier_date, false)
    )                                                           as has_timestamp_anomaly
